kimi_k3/001:
The strategy combines:

- Adaptive iterative-deepening negamax search with alpha-beta pruning.
- Queen-distance territory evaluation: empty squares reachable sooner by one color count toward that color.
- Mobility evaluation, adjusted by game phase.
- Move ordering based on central control and proximity to opponent amazons.
- A move-width limit at deeper levels plus a strict time guard.
- A fully generated legal fallback move, ensuring a valid move is returned even if search is interrupted.
kimi_k3/002:
Strategy: I always control the `1` amazons. I use a strong territory evaluation: for every empty square I compute (via two small BFS over queen‑lines through empty cells) the minimum number of moves each side needs to reach it. A square is scored to the side that reaches it sooner, with a bonus when the opponent cannot reach it at all; tied (contested) squares are awarded to the side to move (tempo). 

Move choice is an exact depth‑1 optimization over *all* legal moves: for each amazon destination I pick the arrow that maximizes the evaluation, then take the global best — so no legal move is overlooked at the base. On top of that I add (time permitting) a cheap "catastrophe" guard that penalizes moves leaving a single critical empty cell the opponent could burn to swing territory, and in late/low‑branching positions (total legal moves ≤ 120) I switch to a bounded iterative‑deepening negamax with alpha‑beta. A hard deadline with a guaranteed already‑computed best move ensures I always return a legal move in time.
kimi_k3/003: The policy uses iterative-deepening alpha-beta search under a strict time budget. Evaluation is based on queen-move territory distance to empty squares, raw amazon mobility, and large penalties for amazons with no moves. Moves are ordered by centralization and by shooting arrows near enemy amazons; a Zobrist transposition table and evaluation cache improve deeper iterations. If anything goes wrong or time expires, it still returns a legal move from the generated move list.
kimi_k3/004: Strategy: exhaustive 1‑ply search over *all* legal (amazon move + arrow) moves, scored by a strong Amazons heuristic. The evaluation combines (a) a “minimum queen‑moves” territory map computed with two multi‑source BFS (who can reach each empty square first), (b) raw amazon mobility difference, and (c) reachable‑empty‑square difference. Shooting the arrow is part of each candidate, so the search naturally picks arrows that wall off the opponent. Instant wins (opponent left with no amazon move) return a huge score. A hard time deadline (with a guaranteed already‑evaluated best move) and ordering candidate arrows by centrality make the policy both safe and always legal; if anything goes wrong it still emits a syntactically valid move.
kimi_k3/005: The strategy is to combine a strong Amazons heuristic with selective alpha-beta search. The evaluator uses multi-source queen-move distance territory (only arrows are permanent blockers), real amazon mobility, adjacent liberties, and small center/tempo terms. At the root I generate all legal moves, immediately take any move that leaves the opponent with no amazon move, order the rest by a fast mobility heuristic, fully evaluate the best candidates, then deepen only the most promising moves with time-checked alpha-beta. A fallback always emits a syntactically valid move, and normal move generation only emits legal move/arrow pairs.
